The holding that travelled to Washington

ACT_2.quote: as a matter of public policy under West Virginia law, an arbitration clause in a nursing home admission agreement adopted prior to an occurrence of negligence that results in a personal injury or wrongful death, shall not be enforced to compel arbitration of a dispute concerning the negligence.
ACT_2.attribution: The Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia, quoted in Marmet (2012), Part I (Pet. App. 85a–86a)

ACT_2.secondary: 'often fraught with urgency, confusion, and stress' — Brown I, quoted in Brown II, n. 20

ACT_2.quote: People seek medical care in a nursing home for long-term treatment to heal, and do so only a few times in life. Nursing homes daily sign contracts with patients as a routine course of doing business.
ACT_2.attribution: Brown II (2012) — the state court's own sentences, written after the remand

ACT_2.quote: The doctrine of unconscionability means that, because of an overall and gross imbalance, one-sidedness or lop-sidedness in a contract, a court may be justified in refusing to enforce the contract as written.
ACT_2.attribution: Brown I, Syllabus Point 12, quoted in Brown II (2012), n. 22

ACT_2.quote: the courts of this State are not hostile to arbitration or to adhesion contracts. We are hostile toward contracts of adhesion that are unconscionable and rely upon arbitration as an artifice to defraud a weaker party of rights clearly provided by the common law or statute.
ACT_2.attribution: The Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia, quoted in Brown II (2012), n. 19

ACT_2.quote: A contract of adhesion is one drafted and imposed by a party of superior strength that leaves the subscribing party little or no opportunity to alter the substantive terms, and only the opportunity to adhere to the contract or reject it.
ACT_2.attribution: Brown I, Syllabus Point 18, quoted in Brown II (2012), n. 35

ACT_2.quote: [f]inding that there is an adhesion contract is the beginning point for analysis, not the end of it; what courts aim at doing is distinguishing good adhesion contracts which should be enforced from bad adhesion contracts which should not.
ACT_2.attribution: State ex rel. Dunlap v. Berger (2002), quoted in Brown II (2012), n. 36

ACT_2.quote: It may be disingenuous for a nursing home to later assert that the patient or family member consciously, knowingly and deliberately accepted an arbitration clause in the contract, and understood the clause was intended to eliminate their access to the courts if the nursing home negligently injured or killed the patient.
ACT_2.attribution: Brown II (2012) — the state court's own sentence

ACT_2.secondary: Two petitions for certiorari. The defendants specifically challenged Syllabus Point 21.

ACT_3.quote: With tendentious reasoning, the United States Supreme Court has stretched the application of the FAA from being a procedural statutory scheme effective only in the federal courts, to being a substantive law that preempts state law in both the federal and state courts.
ACT_3.attribution: Brown I (2011), quoted in Brown II (2012), n. 14

ACT_3.secondary: The state court read the text and the congressional history as a scheme for commercial entities engaged in interstate commerce

ACT_3.quote: Congress did not intend for the FAA to be, in any way, applicable to personal injury or wrongful death suits that only collaterally derive from a written agreement that evidences a transaction affecting interstate commerce
ACT_3.attribution: The Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia, quoted in Marmet (2012), Part I (Pet. App. 84a)

ACT_3.quote: State and federal courts must enforce the Federal Arbitration Act (FAA), 9 U. S. C. §1 et seq., with respect to all arbitration agreements covered by that statute.
ACT_3.attribution: Marmet Health Care Center, Inc. v. Brown (2012) (per curiam) — the opinion's first sentence

ACT_3.quote: The state court held unenforceable all predispute arbitration agreements that apply to claims alleging personal injury or wrongful death against nursing homes.

written provision in . . . a contract evidencing a transaction involving commerce to settle by arbitration a controversy thereafter arising out of such contract or transaction . . . shall be valid, irrevocable, and enforceable, save upon such grounds as exist at law or in equity for the revocation of any contract.
ACT_3.attribution: 9 U. S. C. §2, quoted in Marmet (2012), Part I

ACT_3.quote: [w]hen state law prohibits outright the arbitration of a particular type of claim, the analysis is straightforward: The conflicting rule is displaced by the FAA.
ACT_3.attribution: AT&T Mobility LLC v. Concepcion (2011), quoted in Marmet (2012), Part I

ACT_3.quote: West Virginia's prohibition against predispute agreements to arbitrate personal-injury or wrongful-death claims against nursing homes is a categorical rule prohibiting arbitration of a particular type of claim, and that rule is contrary to the terms and coverage of the FAA.
The West Virginia court's interpretation of the FAA was both incorrect and inconsistent with clear instruction in the precedents of this Court.
When this Court has fulfilled its duty to interpret federal law, a state court may not contradict or fail to implement the rule so established.
ACT_3.attribution: Marmet (2012) (per curiam), citing U. S. Const., Art. VI, cl. 2

ACT_5.quote: In accordance with the Supreme Court's mandate, we overrule Syllabus Point 21 of Brown I. We otherwise find that the Supreme Court's decision does not counsel us to alter our original analysis of West Virginia's common law of contracts.
ACT_5.attribution: Brown II, 229 W. Va. 382 (2012), Ketchum, C.J.

ACT_5.quote: The Supreme Court's opinion did not discuss any other portion of Brown I, aside from Syllabus Point 21 and its accompanying text.
The parties have not challenged our holding in Syllabus Point 11 of Brown I regarding the preemption of Section 15(c) by Section 2 of the FAA, and we need not revisit it.
The doctrine of unconscionability that we explicated in Brown I is a general, state, common-law, contract-law principle that is not specific to arbitration, and does not implicate the FAA.
A contract term is unenforceable if it is both procedurally and substantively unconscionable. However, both need not be present to the same degree.
ACT_5.attribution: Brown I, Syllabus Point 20, quoted in Brown II (2012), n. 32

ACT_5.quote: Agreements to arbitrate must contain at least 'a modicum of bilaterality' to avoid unconscionability.

ACT_5.quote: claims of coercion, fraud, or unequal bargaining power in the formation of an arbitration agreement are 'best left for resolution in specific cases'

ACT_5.quote: The circuit court's order in Brown's case is devoid of any findings of fact or conclusions of law on the question of unconscionability.

We conclude the correct course is to remand these cases to the circuit courts for the taking of evidence, the full development of a record, and proper consideration of whether the clauses are unconscionable.
